newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent ends off in profit-taking, gas oil weake.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent ends off in profit-taking, gas oil weake.

text.p: IPE Brent crude futures ended lower in a round of modest profit-taking in thin volumes following Monday's sharp weather-led rally.
February Brent finished down 19 cents at $23.70 a barrel after a late sell-off counteracted an afternoon recovery led by U.S. gasoline.
"Most people were expecting the market to correct lower today but the Exxon cracker outage just seemed to hold the market up for a while," said an IPE broker.
"But volumes are thin and its not a convincing sell yet," he added. "I wouldn't read too much into it."
Brent got help earlier from news of an outage in a catalytic cracking unit at Exxon's Baton Rouge, Louisiana refinery.
Dealers said news filtering through of more Iraqi export contracts had been pushed into the background.
"It's a factor but people know how much crude to expect and for now opinion is that the market needs it,' said a trader.
Weaker U.S. heating oil helped drag IPE ga oil down undermined by expectations of a build in U.S. distillate stocks in tonight's weekly inventory report.
Most traders were expecting a build in U.S. distillates in this week's oil inventory data from the American Petroleum Institute (API).
Production of distillates was expected to remain near record levels in the U.S., calming fears over rising demand when cold weather arrives later this week.
IPE gas oil ended lower down 50 cents at $222 a tonne for February and off a $1.25 versus February, undercut by lower U.S. heating oil values.
